messages:
From: Ariel Gomez <ariel@hydra.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-11T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Quick sizing help for pilot: traffic & burst shape

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this — Hydra Labs is trying to scope a 6-week pilot to validate latency and unit cost for an LLM feature in our product. We have rough telemetry but would love Redwood's input on fleet sizing before we commit. High-level ask: what GPU footprint do we need for a pilot that supports a 1k concurrent session pilot with heavy burst windows (10x sustained for ~20 minutes twice per day)?

I attached a small CSV with sampled request logs (token counts, timestamps) — please confirm you received it. Also note we expect prompt lengths to be variable: 40–600 tokens; typical response 60–800 tokens. Calls are primarily synchronous (low-latency, user-facing).

Would appreciate a short questionnaire if you need structured answers.

Best,
Ariel
Ariel Gomez
Head of Infrastructure, Hydra Labs
Ariel@hydra.ai
(Attachment: hydra-workload-snapshot.csv)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Ariel Gomez <ariel@hydra.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-11T11:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sizing help for pilot: traffic & burst shape

Hi Ariel — received the CSV, thanks. Quick note: we'll aim to return an initial footprint estimate and a recommended pilot runbook this week. To make the estimate tight, can you fill the short questionnaire below (paste answers inline) — this helps avoid multiple back-and-forths.

1) Traffic shape: avg requests/sec (sustained) and peak requests/sec in the burst windows.
2) Request mix: % chat vs single-turn generation vs embeddings/rerank.
3) Token breakdown: median prompt tokens, 90th, 99th; same for responses.
4) Session model: are sessions stateful (KV cached across turns)? If yes, avg turns per session and KV cache retention time.
5) Desired SLOs: p95 and p99 latency targets, and acceptable P50/P95 token cost threshold if any.
6) Failover policy: if Dedicated not available, is fallback to a smaller hosted model acceptable?
7) Pilot commitment: expected QPS/day and target pilot duration (you mentioned 6 weeks) and budget band for pilot.
8) Any security/compliance constraints (SOC2, data residency, VPC) and whether you'll need Private deployment for pilot.

Attachments: I've attached a small CSV template that helps map token distributions into GPU throughput assumptions (pre-sales-workload-template.csv). If you can return the filled CSV, we can model batching, KV cache impact, and recommended GPU SKUs.

I'll loop Karthik for initial mapping and Marissa to help run the pilot playbook.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: pre-sales-workload-template.csv)

From: Ariel Gomez <ariel@hydra.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-12T08:57:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sizing help for pilot: traffic & burst shape

Thanks — answers inline below and I've attached the filled CSV.

1) Traffic shape: sustained 35 req/sec (writes -> generation calls), burst peak ~350 req/sec for ~20 minutes twice daily (morning + evening). Off-peak ~5 req/sec overnight.
2) Request mix: 70% chat (multi-turn), 20% single-turn gen, 10% rerank/embedding.
3) Token breakdown: median prompt 120 tokens, 90th 420, 99th 780. Responses: median 160, 90th 540, 99th 820.
4) Session model: stateful. Avg turns per session ~4. KV cache retained for session duration (typical 3–8 minutes, some sessions longer).
5) Desired SLOs: p95 latency target 600ms; p99 1.5s. Cost: pilot budget target ~$12k/month on infra (billable).
6) Failover: fallback acceptable to a smaller model if latency degrades, but must be signaled to product so clients can degrade gracefully.
7) Pilot commitment: 6 weeks; expected average QPS/day ~3M calls; critical to validate tail latency under burst.
8) Security: SOC2 required; data residency US. We prefer Dedicated or Private but can start on Dedicated with VPC peering.

(Attachment: hydra-workload-snapshot-filled.csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Ariel Gomez <ariel@hydra.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-12T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Burst horizon & session mapping for Hydra pilot — initial mapping

Thanks for the data, Ariel — useful detail. Quick read and initial mapping below (draft numbers; we'll refine after a short call):

Summary of constraints:
- Sustained load: 35 rps with 1k concurrent active sessions.
- Burst: 350 rps for 20m x2/day, short tail tokens up to ~820 tokens.
- Stateful sessions: KV cache reduces repeated prompt tokens by ~25% on average.

Preliminary sizing assumptions:
- Model: MPT-like 34B (quantized variant) for parity with quality target; if you accept some quality degradation we can propose a 13B variant for cost-savings.
- GPU pick: A100 80GB equivalent (or H100 if available) for lowest latency on 800-token responses.
- Concurrency mapping: expect ~6–8 concurrent request slots per GPU on this model/response mix when using Redwood continuous batching and KV caching. For 350 rps sustained in burst and average generation latency ~450ms, we estimate ~55 concurrent slots needed across service. Accounting for session affinity and headroom, this maps to ~8–10 GPUs for the burst window. For sustained baseline (35 rps) ~2 GPUs.
- Pilot footprint recommendation: reserve 10 GPUs (dedicated) with autoscale policy to add 4 extra GPUs for extreme spikes; enable prefix KV caching and a 25ms batching window.
- Cost estimate (infra only): approximate $9k–$13k/month depending on SKU and region — aligns with your ~$12k target if using A100 reserved pricing.

Open questions (for call):
- Are all requests single-model? Any step that invokes heavy rerank/embed flows server-side?
- Your tolerance for transient latency vs permanent fallback.
- Any peak concurrency higher than 350 rps observed historically?

I've attached a draft capacity mapping workbook that shows per-GPU concurrency math and sensitivity for model size / batching / KV effectiveness. Can we book 30–45 minutes tomorrow to walk through and finalize the mutual action plan?

(Attachment: capacity-mapping-draft.xlsx)

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Pre-Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
